nodes.name: Dhruva Tārā
nodes.summary: The Pole Star (Polaris). The fixed point in the night sky around which all other stars appear to turn.
nodes.story:
Dhruva is the pole star, the fixed point around which the heavens appear to turn. According to the Bhagavata Purana, the young boy Dhruva performed intense tapas and was granted the position of the immovable star by Vishnu.

Interesting fact: The complete narrative of Dhruva's austerities and his attainment of the pole star is given in the Bhagavata Purana, Canto 4, Chapters 8–12.

nodes.name: Brahma
nodes.summary: The Creator, first of the Trimurti.

nodes.name: Vishnu
nodes.summary: The Preserver, second of the Trimurti.

nodes.name: Shiva
nodes.summary: The Destroyer/Transformer, third of the Trimurti.

nodes.name: Atri
nodes.summary: One of the Saptarishi (Seven Sages) of the current Manvantara. Also traditionally identified with the star Megrez in Ursa Major.
nodes.story:
The Saptarishi are the seven great sages who uphold the cosmic order and preserve the Vedas across the ages. In the present Manvantara they are: Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulaha, Pulastya, Kratu, and Vashishtha (with variations in lists across texts).

They form the asterism known in the West as the Big Dipper.

Interesting fact: The Puranas consistently describe the Saptarishi as the seven sages who preserve the Vedas and uphold dharma in every Manvantara.

nodes.summary: One of the Saptarishi (Seven Sages) of the current Manvantara.

nodes.name: Jamadagni
nodes.summary: One of the Saptarishi (Seven Sages) of the current Manvantara.

nodes.name: Kashyapa
nodes.summary: One of the Saptarishi (Seven Sages) of the current Manvantara.

nodes.name: Vashishtha
nodes.summary: One of the Saptarishi (Seven Sages) of the current Manvantara. Also traditionally identified with the star Mizar in Ursa Major (with his wife Arundhati as the companion star Alcor).

nodes.name: Aditi
nodes.summary: Mother of the Adityas; consort of Kashyapa.

nodes.name: Ashwini Kumaras
nodes.summary: Twin horse-headed physician gods of the Devas.

nodes.name: Yama
nodes.summary: God of death and dharma; judge of the dead.

nodes.name: Agni
nodes.summary: God of fire, the divine messenger between humans and gods.

nodes.name: Chandra
nodes.summary: The Moon, also called Soma. Governs the mind, emotion, and the mother in Vedic astrology; waxes and wanes as it circles the Earth roughly once a month. Presiding deity of Mrigashira.
nodes.story:
Chandra is the mind, the reflector of light, and the nourisher of life. He rules the tides of emotion and the cycles of growth.

Interesting fact: Puranic tradition, including accounts in the Mahabharata, states that Chandra married the 27 Nakshatras and loved Rohini most.

nodes.name: Rudra
nodes.summary: Fierce storm form of Shiva.

nodes.name: Guru (Brihaspati)
nodes.symbol: Staff and manuscript, rides an elephant
nodes.summary: Jupiter. Preceptor of the Devas; governs wisdom, teaching, and fortune -- traditionally the most benefic of the Navagraha. Presiding deity of Pushya.
nodes.story:
Brihaspati is the guru of the gods, the planet of wisdom, expansion, and dharma.

Interesting fact: Brihaspati is portrayed in the Vedas and Puranas as the preceptor of the gods and the guardian of sacred wisdom.

nodes.name: Sarpa
nodes.summary: The serpent deity, associated with the Nagas.

nodes.name: Pitris
nodes.summary: The divine ancestors.

nodes.name: Bhaga
nodes.summary: Aditya of prosperity, marital bliss and good fortune.

nodes.name: Aryaman
nodes.summary: Aditya of contracts, honour and unions.

nodes.name: Savitar
nodes.summary: Aditya of the sun before sunrise, the impeller.

nodes.name: Vishvakarma
nodes.summary: Divine architect and craftsman of the gods.

nodes.name: Vayu
nodes.summary: God of wind and breath.

nodes.name: Indra
nodes.summary: King of the Devas, wielder of the vajra.

nodes.name: Mitra
nodes.summary: Aditya of friendship, contracts and covenants.

nodes.name: Nirriti
nodes.summary: Goddess of dissolution and destruction.

nodes.name: Apah
nodes.summary: Deity of the cosmic waters.

nodes.name: Vishvadevas
nodes.summary: The collective of Universal Gods.

nodes.name: Ashta Vasu
nodes.summary: The eight elemental gods of natural phenomena.

nodes.name: Varuna
nodes.summary: God of cosmic and earthly waters, keeper of cosmic order.

nodes.name: Aja Ekapada
nodes.summary: The one-footed goat, a fierce form associated with lightning.

nodes.name: Ahirbudhnya
nodes.summary: The serpent of the deep, guardian of hidden wisdom.

nodes.name: Pushan
nodes.summary: Aditya who nourishes and protects travellers and animals.

nodes.name: Ashwini
nodes.summary: The healer — swift beginnings and new starts.
nodes.story:
Ashwini is the first of the 27 Nakshatras, ruled by the Ashwini Kumaras — the twin divine physicians of the gods. Its symbol is a horse's head.

This Nakshatra marks beginnings, swift movement, and the power of healing. The Ashwini Kumaras are known for restoring youth and health, even bringing the dead back to life in the Vedic accounts.

Interesting fact: The Ashwini Kumaras are frequently praised in the Rigveda (especially mandala 1) as the divine twin physicians who bring healing and restore youth.

nodes.name: Bharani
nodes.summary: The bearer — restraint, transformation and the boundary of life.
nodes.story:
Bharani is ruled by Yama, the lord of dharma and death. Its symbol is the yoni, representing the gateway of birth and the restraint of creative force.

This Nakshatra carries the dual power of creation and containment. It teaches the necessity of discipline over desire and the sacredness of limits.

Interesting fact: Classical Jyotisha works, including the Brihat Samhita of Varahamihira, associate Bharani with Yama and the principle of restraint.

nodes.name: Krittika
nodes.summary: The cutter — sharp purification and burning away illusion.
nodes.story:
Krittika is ruled by Agni, the god of fire. Its symbol is a razor or sharp flame.

This Nakshatra burns away impurities and reveals what is essential. It is associated with the nurturing fire that both cooks and purifies. The six Krittikas (nurses of Kartikeya) are also remembered here.

Interesting fact: Both the Rigveda and later Jyotisha tradition identify Krittika with the Pleiades and the sharp, purifying nature of Agni.

nodes.name: Rohini
nodes.summary: The ascender — growth, fertility and creative beauty.
nodes.story:
Rohini is ruled by Prajapati (Brahma) or the Moon in some traditions. Its symbol is an ox-cart or chariot.

This is the Nakshatra of growth, beauty, and fertility. Rohini is described as the favorite of the Moon, who spends the most time with her among all the Nakshatras.

Interesting fact: The Mahabharata and several Puranas describe Rohini as the most beloved of Chandra's 27 wives, the Nakshatras.

nodes.name: Mrigashira
nodes.summary: The searcher — gentle curiosity and quiet pursuit.
nodes.story:
Mrigashira is ruled by Soma (the Moon). Its symbol is a deer's head.

This Nakshatra represents the searching mind and the gentle, wandering quality of curiosity. The deer is ever alert, ever seeking the next pasture.

Interesting fact: Traditional Nakshatra texts symbolize Mrigashira with a deer's head and place it under the rulership of Soma.

nodes.name: Ardra
nodes.summary: The moist one — storms that clear the way for renewal.
nodes.story:
Ardra is ruled by Rudra, the fierce form of Shiva. Its symbol is a teardrop or diamond.

This Nakshatra carries the storm that clears the air. It is linked to intense emotion, destruction of the old, and the tears that precede renewal.

Interesting fact: Ardra is linked to Rudra in classical Jyotisha literature, its teardrop symbol signifying the purifying storm.

nodes.name: Punarvasu
nodes.summary: The return of the light — renewal after hardship.
nodes.story:
Punarvasu is ruled by Aditi, the mother of the Adityas. Its symbol is a quiver of arrows or a bow.

The name means "return of the light" or "renewal of the good." It represents the restoration of what was lost and the second chance.

Interesting fact: The name Punarvasu is explained in traditional Nakshatra descriptions as "the return of the light," signifying restoration.

nodes.name: Pushya
nodes.summary: The nourisher — the most auspicious of the Nakshatras.
nodes.story:
Pushya is ruled by Brihaspati, the guru of the gods. Its symbol is a flower, a circle, or a cow's udder.

This is one of the most auspicious Nakshatras, associated with nourishment, wisdom, and the protective care of a mother.

Interesting fact: Varahamihira's Brihat Samhita and later muhurta texts regard Pushya as one of the most auspicious of all Nakshatras.

nodes.name: Ashlesha
nodes.summary: The embracer — hypnotic wisdom and hidden intent.
nodes.story:
Ashlesha is ruled by the Nagas (serpent deities). Its symbol is a coiled serpent.

This Nakshatra holds the power of kundalini, deep intuition, and the embrace that can either protect or constrict. It is intense and penetrating.

Interesting fact: Classical sources associate Ashlesha with the Nagas, and its symbol of the coiled serpent points to latent transformative power.

nodes.name: Magha
nodes.summary: The mighty one — ancestry, legacy and inherited power.
nodes.story:
Magha is ruled by the Pitris (ancestral fathers). Its symbol is a royal throne.

This Nakshatra connects the living to the lineage of ancestors. It carries dignity, authority, and the weight of inherited responsibility.

Interesting fact: Magha is ruled by the Pitris according to traditional Jyotisha, and is described as the Nakshatra of ancestral authority and dignity.

nodes.name: Purva Phalguni
nodes.summary: The former reddish one — pleasure, rest and good fortune.
nodes.story:
Purva Phalguni is ruled by Bhaga, the god of enjoyment and marital bliss. Its symbol is the front legs of a bed or hammock.

This Nakshatra governs pleasure, creativity, and the delight of union. It is playful yet sacred.

Interesting fact: Traditional texts assign Purva Phalguni to Bhaga and symbolize it with the front legs of the marriage bed.

nodes.name: Uttara Phalguni
nodes.summary: The latter reddish one — bonds of friendship and patronage.
nodes.story:
Uttara Phalguni is ruled by Aryaman, the god of patronage and contracts. Its symbol is the back legs of a bed.

This Nakshatra brings lasting alliances, generosity, and the formalization of relationships.

Interesting fact: Uttara Phalguni is linked to Aryaman and is frequently recommended in classical muhurta literature for marriage and lasting bonds.

nodes.name: Hasta
nodes.summary: The hand — skill, craft and the power to grasp opportunity.
nodes.story:
Hasta is ruled by Savitar, the creative aspect of the Sun. Its symbol is an open hand.

This Nakshatra represents skill, craftsmanship, and the power of the hand to create and heal.

Interesting fact: Hasta is ruled by Savitar in the classical Nakshatra system and represents the skillful, creative power of the hand.

nodes.name: Chitra
nodes.summary: The brilliant one — artistry and divine craftsmanship.
nodes.story:
Chitra is ruled by Tvashtar, the divine architect. Its symbol is a bright pearl or jewel.

This Nakshatra is the artisan of the sky, governing beauty, design, and the sudden flash of inspiration.

Interesting fact: Chitra is governed by Tvashtar, the celestial architect, and is traditionally connected with the bright star Spica.

nodes.name: Swati
nodes.symbol: Young shoot swaying in the wind
nodes.summary: The independent one — movement, trade and self-reliance.
nodes.story:
Swati is ruled by Vayu, the god of wind. Its symbol is a young plant or sprout.

This Nakshatra carries independence, flexibility, and the ability to move freely without losing one's center.

Interesting fact: Swati is ruled by Vayu in traditional lists and is symbolized by a tender plant, indicating independence and adaptability.

nodes.name: Vishakha
nodes.summary: The forked branch — determined pursuit of a goal.
nodes.story:
Vishakha is ruled jointly by Indra and Agni. Its symbol is a triumphal arch or decorated gateway.

This Nakshatra represents focused purpose, determination, and the successful completion of a goal.

Interesting fact: Vishakha is jointly ruled by Indra and Agni, and classical descriptions emphasize its quality of determined achievement.

nodes.name: Anuradha
nodes.summary: The follower of Radha — devotion, friendship and success through cooperation.
nodes.story:
Anuradha is ruled by Mitra, the god of friendship and contracts. Its symbol is a staff or triumphal gateway.

This Nakshatra governs devotion, friendship, and the quiet strength of loyalty.

Interesting fact: Anuradha is ruled by Mitra and is praised in traditional sources for fostering friendship and loyal alliances.

nodes.name: Jyeshtha
nodes.summary: The eldest — seniority, protection and quiet authority.
nodes.story:
Jyeshtha is ruled by Indra, the king of the gods. Its symbol is an earring or royal umbrella.

This is the Nakshatra of the elder, of seniority, and of protective authority.

Interesting fact: Jyeshtha, ruled by Indra, is described in classical texts as the Nakshatra of the elder and of protective seniority.

nodes.name: Mula
nodes.summary: The root — getting to the foundation by uprooting what came before.
nodes.story:
Mula is ruled by Nirriti, the goddess of dissolution. Its symbol is a bundle of roots.

This Nakshatra goes to the root of things — both the foundation and the uprooting of what no longer serves.

Interesting fact: Mula is ruled by Nirriti and is symbolized by a cluster of roots, representing both the foundation and the act of uprooting.

nodes.name: Purva Ashadha
nodes.summary: The former invincible one — early, unstoppable conviction.
nodes.story:
Purva Ashadha is ruled by the Apas (water deities). Its symbol is an elephant tusk or fan.

This Nakshatra carries invincible energy and the purification of water. It is associated with early victory.

Interesting fact: Purva Ashadha is associated with the waters (Apas) and is traditionally said to confer invincible strength.

nodes.name: Uttara Ashadha
nodes.symbol: Elephant tusk / planks of a bed
nodes.summary: The latter invincible one — lasting victory earned through universal support.
nodes.story:
Uttara Ashadha is ruled by the Vishvedevas. Its symbol is an elephant tusk or the planks of a bed.

This Nakshatra represents final victory, enduring success, and universal support.

Interesting fact: Uttara Ashadha is ruled by the Vishvedevas and is regarded as a Nakshatra of lasting victory in classical sources.

nodes.name: Shravana
nodes.summary: The listener — learning, memory and connection through hearing.
nodes.story:
Shravana is ruled by Vishnu. Its symbol is three footprints or an ear.

This Nakshatra governs listening, learning, and the sacred path of knowledge. The three steps of Vishnu are remembered here.

Interesting fact: Shravana is ruled by Vishnu and is linked both to the three strides of Vishnu and to the power of attentive listening.

nodes.name: Dhanishta
nodes.summary: The wealthiest — rhythm, prosperity and celebration.
nodes.story:
Dhanishta is ruled by the Vasus. Its symbol is a drum or flute.

This Nakshatra carries rhythm, wealth, and the music of the spheres. It is associated with abundance that flows through proper timing.

Interesting fact: Dhanishta is ruled by the Vasus and is associated in tradition with rhythm, prosperity, and cosmic order.

nodes.name: Shatabhisha
nodes.summary: The hundred healers — mystery, healing and cosmic law.
nodes.story:
Shatabhisha is ruled by Varuna. Its symbol is an empty circle or a hundred physicians.

This Nakshatra governs healing, mystery, and the vastness of the ocean of consciousness.

Interesting fact: Shatabhisha is ruled by Varuna and is described as the Nakshatra of healing and the vast, enclosing circle.

nodes.name: Purva Bhadrapada
nodes.symbol: Front legs of a funeral cot
nodes.summary: The former auspicious feet — intense transformation through fire.
nodes.story:
Purva Bhadrapada is ruled by Aja Ekapada. Its symbol is the front legs of a funeral cot.

This Nakshatra carries intense, dualistic energy and the transformation that comes through crisis.

Interesting fact: Purva Bhadrapada is ruled by Aja Ekapada and carries the intense, purifying fire linked to the front of the funeral cot.

nodes.name: Uttara Bhadrapada
nodes.symbol: Back legs of a funeral cot
nodes.summary: The latter auspicious feet — deep wisdom held in stillness.
nodes.story:
Uttara Bhadrapada is ruled by Ahir Budhnya (the serpent of the deep). Its symbol is the back legs of a funeral cot.

This Nakshatra brings depth, wisdom from the depths, and the calm after transformation.

Interesting fact: Uttara Bhadrapada is ruled by Ahir Budhnya, the serpent of the deep, and signifies profound stillness after transformation.

nodes.name: Revati
nodes.summary: The wealthy wanderer — safe passage and nourishment at the journey's end.
nodes.story:
Revati is ruled by Pushan, the nourisher. Its symbol is a pair of fish or a drum.

This is the final Nakshatra, governing safe journeys, nourishment, and the completion of cycles.

Interesting fact: Revati is ruled by Pushan and is traditionally considered especially protective for those undertaking journeys.

nodes.name: Swayambhuva Manu
nodes.summary: The first Manu; Dhruva's grandfather.

nodes.name: Shatarupa
nodes.summary: Consort of Swayambhuva Manu; Dhruva's grandmother.

nodes.name: Uttanapada
nodes.summary: King, son of Swayambhuva Manu; Dhruva's father.

nodes.name: Suniti
nodes.summary: Elder queen of Uttanapada; Dhruva's mother.

nodes.name: Suruchi
nodes.summary: Younger, favoured queen of Uttanapada; Uttama's mother.

nodes.name: Uttama
nodes.summary: Son of Suruchi; Dhruva's half-brother.

nodes.name: Dhruva
nodes.summary: Prince who, through penance, was granted an unmoving place in the sky by Vishnu.

nodes.name: Narada
nodes.summary: Celestial sage who guided young Dhruva toward his penance.

nodes.name: Dhruva's Penance
nodes.summary: Wounded by Suruchi's rejection, Dhruva undertakes fierce penance in the forest, guided by Narada, until Vishnu grants him an eternal place in the heavens.

nodes.name: Surya
nodes.summary: The Sun. Solar deity and source of all life; governs the soul, vitality, and the father in Vedic astrology. Chief of the Navagraha and the brightest object in the sky.
nodes.story:
Surya is the soul of the solar system and the visible form of the divine light. He is the giver of life, clarity, and authority.

In the Vedic tradition, Surya is both the physical Sun and the inner light of consciousness.

Interesting fact: The celebrated Gayatri Mantra (Rigveda 3.62.10) is addressed to Savitar, an aspect of Surya, as the awakener of the intellect.

nodes.name: Mangala
nodes.summary: Mars, also called Kuja or Angaraka. Son of the Earth goddess Bhumi; the red planet, governing courage, conflict, and energy.
nodes.story:
Mangala is the energy of action, courage, and decisive force. He is the commander among the Grahas.

Interesting fact: Classical Jyotisha associates Mangala with fiery energy, courage, and decisive action.

nodes.name: Budha
nodes.symbol: Sword and shield, rides a lion
nodes.summary: Mercury. Son of Chandra and Tara; governs intellect, communication, and commerce -- the swiftest planet, never far from the Sun in the sky.
nodes.story:
Budha is the prince of intelligence, communication, and discrimination. He is the fast-moving messenger.

Interesting fact: Puranic accounts describe Budha as the son of Chandra and the planet governing intelligence and discrimination.

nodes.name: Shukra
nodes.summary: Venus. Preceptor of the Asuras; governs beauty, love, and material wealth -- the brightest planet, often visible near dawn or dusk.
nodes.story:
Shukra is the teacher of the Asuras, the planet of beauty, love, and refined pleasure.

Interesting fact: According to Puranic tradition, Shukra possesses the Sanjivani Vidya — the knowledge that can restore the dead to life.

nodes.name: Shani
nodes.symbol: Rides a crow, holds a bow
nodes.summary: Saturn. Son of Surya and his shadow-wife Chhaya; governs discipline, karma, and delay -- the slowest-moving and most feared of the Navagraha.
nodes.story:
Shani is the lord of time, discipline, and the consequences of action. He is the slowest and most serious of the Grahas.

Interesting fact: Traditional sources describe Shani as the son of Surya and the planet that delivers the fruits of karma over time.

nodes.name: Rahu
nodes.summary: The Moon's ascending (north) node. Half of the demon Svarbhanu, decapitated by Vishnu's Mohini avatar after stealing a taste of amrita; governs obsession, illusion, and eclipses.
nodes.story:
Rahu is the north lunar node, the head of the dragon, representing worldly desire and unconventional paths.

Interesting fact: The Puranas recount that Rahu causes eclipses by attempting to devour the Sun and the Moon after the Samudra Manthana.

nodes.name: Ketu
nodes.summary: The Moon's descending (south) node, always 180 degrees from Rahu. The other half of the same severed demon; governs detachment and spiritual liberation.
nodes.story:
Ketu is the south lunar node, the tail of the dragon, representing detachment, moksha, and past-life mastery.

Interesting fact: Ketu is described as the severed body of the demon who tasted the amrita, and is linked with detachment and liberation.

nodes.name: Akash Ganga
nodes.summary: The celestial river of light -- the Milky Way arching across the night sky.
nodes.story:
Akash Ganga is the celestial form of the sacred river Ganga — the Milky Way stretching across the night sky. In tradition it is the path of the gods and the luminous river that flows through the heavens.

Interesting fact: Traditional Indian sources identify the Milky Way as Akash Ganga, the celestial form of the sacred river Ganga.
